nodes.content: Develop long-tail image recognition that preserves rare-class accuracy when predictive background correlations reverse without target-domain labels.
requirements: Improve bottom-quintile class macro-accuracy by 5 percentage points over empirical risk minimization under background reversals.
Keep top-quintile class macro-accuracy within 1 percentage point of that baseline using identical training data.

nodes.content: Train TailSwap using self-supervised foreground masks for tail-weighted background swaps and head-class distillation from same-data ERM.
How much foreground-mask error can TailSwap tolerate before background swaps erase discriminative rare-class features?
Under reversed backgrounds, TailSwap gains ≥5 tail-accuracy points versus ERM without >1-point head loss when foreground-mask false-negative rate ≤10%.
Sweep 0–30% foreground-mask false negatives during TailSwap training; compare reversed-background tail/head macro-accuracy with same-data ERM.
Run LT-CUB-Rev mask-error sweep (0%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%); compare TailSwap's reversed-background tail/head macro-accuracy to same-data ERM.
LT-CUB-Rev: at 10% mask misses, TailSwap tail/head macro-accuracy reached 43.1%/81.5% versus ERM's 37.8%/82.1%; at 20%, tail fell to 41.0%.
Advance TailSwap only with ≤10% foreground-mask false negatives; 20% errors reduce the tail gain below five points.
Calibrate TailSwap masks for ≤10% foreground misses on source-only cutouts, then measure LT-iNat-Rev tail/head macro-accuracy against same-data ERM.
LT-iNat-Rev report with source-calibrated mask miss rates and TailSwap-versus-ERM tail/head macro-accuracy under reversed backgrounds.
Repeat the LT-CUB-Rev mask-error sweep without head distillation; compare reversed-background tail/head macro-accuracy against TailSwap and same-data ERM.
On LT-CUB-Rev at 10% mask misses, removing distillation yielded 43.4% tail and 79.7% head macro-accuracy versus TailSwap's 43.1%/81.5%.
Dilating foreground masks by eight pixels restores TailSwap's ≥5-point tail gain at 20% mask misses without exceeding one-point head loss.
Train LT-CUB-Rev TailSwap with 0-, 4-, and 8-pixel mask dilation at 20% mask misses; evaluate reversed-background tail/head macro-accuracy.
At 20% mask misses, eight-pixel dilation yielded 42.3% tail and 81.3% head macro-accuracy versus ERM's 37.8%/82.1%.
Replicate eight-pixel dilation at 20% mask misses on LT-iNat-Rev; compare tail/head macro-accuracy with undilated TailSwap and same-data ERM.
LT-iNat-Rev at 20% misses: eight-pixel dilation tail/head macro-accuracy 35.2%/76.0%, undilated 33.9%/76.2%, ERM 29.8%/76.7%.
Train CoreGuard with mask-uncertainty-weighted foreground pooling, rare-class contrastive loss, and ERM head-logit distillation using source images only.
Does CoreGuard's uncertainty-weighted pooling suppress diagnostic tail-class features when small foreground parts receive low mask confidence?
On LT-CUB-Rev, CoreGuard loses ≥3 tail macro-accuracy points versus uniform pooling when diagnostic parts receive <0.5 mask confidence.
Stratify LT-CUB-Rev classes by source-part mask confidence; compare CoreGuard against uniform pooling on reversed-background tail accuracy.
On LT-CUB-Rev, bin tail classes by source diagnostic-part mask confidence below versus above 0.5; compare CoreGuard and uniform-pooling accuracy.
LT-CUB-Rev low-confidence tail classes: CoreGuard scored 38.4% versus uniform pooling's 42.0% macro-accuracy; high-confidence classes scored 45.0% versus 44.5%.
Use uniform pooling when diagnostic-part confidence is below 0.5; retain uncertainty weighting otherwise to avoid the observed 3.6-point tail loss.
Train CoreGuard with uniform pooling below 0.5 source-part confidence on LT-iNat-Rev; compare reversed-background tail/head macro-accuracy against same-data ERM.
CoreGuard LT-iNat-Rev evaluation sheet listing source-part confidence bins, adaptive pooling settings, and reversed-background tail/head macro-accuracy versus ERM.
Train ClusterGuard with source-only background pseudo-environments, class-conditional tail-weighted group DRO, and ERM head-logit distillation.
With ≥80% source background-cluster purity, ClusterGuard gains ≥5 tail points and loses ≤1 head point versus ERM on LT-iNat-Rev.
Measure source pseudo-environment purity using held-out source background tags; evaluate ≥80%-purity ClusterGuard against same-data ERM on LT-iNat-Rev tail/head macro-accuracy.
On LT-iNat-Rev, 84%-pure ClusterGuard scored 34.0% tail and 76.1% head macro-accuracy versus ERM's 29.8%/76.7%.
Sweep ClusterGuard tail-group DRO weights 1, 2, and 4 with 84%-pure source clusters; retest LT-iNat-Rev against ERM.
At tail-group weight 2, 84%-pure ClusterGuard reached 35.1% tail and 75.9% head macro-accuracy on LT-iNat-Rev versus ERM's 29.8%/76.7%.
Does ClusterGuard retain its ≥5-point tail gain when rare classes span fewer than three source background clusters?
Stratify 84%-pure LT-iNat-Rev tail classes by <3 versus ≥3 source clusters; compare weight-2 ClusterGuard, initial ClusterGuard, and ERM.
Stratify 84%-pure LT-iNat-Rev tail classes by <3 versus ≥3 source clusters; compare initial and weight-2 ClusterGuard macro-accuracy against ERM.
LT-iNat-Rev cluster-support audit listing source-cluster counts and <3/≥3 tail macro-accuracy for initial ClusterGuard, weight-2 ClusterGuard, and ERM.
Train PairAlign with source-only cross-background, same-class tail contrastive pairs and ERM head-logit distillation.
Do cross-background positive pairs with mismatched bird poses weaken PairAlign’s fine-grained tail-class discrimination?
On LT-CUB-Rev, cross-background pairs with keypoint pose similarity <0.4 reduce tail macro-accuracy ≥3 points versus pose-matched pairs.
Train PairAlign on equal-count LT-CUB-Rev cross-background pairs with pose similarity <0.4 versus ≥0.4; compare reversed-background tail macro-accuracy.
LT-CUB-Rev PairAlign tail macro-accuracy was 39.8% with pose similarity <0.4 versus 43.2% with ≥0.4 cross-background pairs.
Restrict PairAlign positives to pose similarity ≥0.4; mismatched poses cost 3.4 tail macro-accuracy points on LT-CUB-Rev.
Evaluate pose-filtered versus unfiltered PairAlign across three LT-CUB-Rev seeds, reporting tail/head macro-accuracy against same-data ERM.
Three-seed LT-CUB-Rev PairAlign comparison table with pose-filtered and unfiltered tail/head macro-accuracy, ERM baseline, and seed-level confidence intervals.
Train ContextAdv with source-only background crops, tail-weighted adversarial background prediction from object embeddings, and ERM head-logit distillation.
Tune ContextAdv adversarial weight on source validation, then compare reversed-background tail/head macro-accuracy with same-data ERM on LT-CUB-Rev and LT-iNat-Rev.
Audit n39’s tail/head confidence intervals against held-out predictions; benchmark source-tuned ContextAdv versus ERM on LT-CUB-Rev and LT-iNat-Rev.
n39 intervals passed audit; ContextAdv tail/head reached 43.0%/81.5% versus ERM’s 37.8%/82.1% on LT-CUB-Rev, and 35.0%/76.0% versus 29.8%/76.7% on LT-iNat-Rev.
Using n32’s support bins and n42’s benchmarks, test ContextAdv versus ERM tail/head macro-accuracy for <3 versus ≥3 source clusters.
LT-iNat-Rev tail macro-accuracy: ContextAdv versus ERM was 34.2% versus 29.1% for <3 clusters, and 35.8% versus 30.5% for ≥3.
Advance ContextAdv: both reversal benchmarks meet tail/head targets, with tail gains persisting across sparse and well-supported source-cluster bins.
Run three-seed ContextAdv evaluations on unseen LT-CUB-Rev and LT-iNat-Rev backgrounds; report tail/head macro-accuracy differences versus same-data ERM.
ContextAdv replication package with three-seed LT-CUB-Rev/LT-iNat-Rev tail/head macro-accuracy tables, source-only training configuration, and matched ERM checkpoints.
